function: Dense Transformer network maps sCSI to auxiliary variables of the closed-form multi-satellite distributed precoder (MS-JoCDWM-DL), maximizing expected sum rate; p. 8-9.
system: Downlink OFDM, 5 cooperating LEO satellites at 600 km, each UPA 10x10, single-antenna UTs (12-48), 2 GHz carrier, 20 MHz bandwidth; no RIS; p. 3, 11.
method: Tensor-equivariant dense Transformer network (3 blocks, D = 32, dynamic tanh), supervised with scale-invariant NMSE loss against labels (A*, u*); closed-form precoder follows; p. 8-11.
data_channel: QuaDRiGa NTN Urban LOS scenario, Walker-Delta constellation; 5000 samples (4500 train, 500 validation, 50 test), random cooperation regions, seven power levels; p. 10-11.
test_conditions: Trained at S = 5 satellites, K = 48 users, 10x10 antennas, 20-50 dBm; tested with S 3-11, K 12-48, NT 8x8-12x12 (Figs. 9-11); p. 10-12.
baselines: Non-learned: single-satellite MMSE and WMMSE (SS-M, SS-WM), separate multi-satellite WMMSE (MS-SepWM), MS-JoWM, proposed MS-JoCDWM. No earlier learned method compared; p. 11.
metrics: Average expected sum rate (bits/channel use) versus power, kappa, phase-error variance, S, K, NT; per-UT rate CDF and violins; running time; p. 11-13.
complexity: Table II: MS-JoCDWM-DL order O(NT^3 K S^3 + LD(K^2 + S^2)), parameters O(D^2); CPU running time in Fig. 13; p. 9, 13.
openness: none; no code or data link in the paper.
q1_support: p. 10: "the channel parameters are generated with the simulator under its" QuaDRiGa NTN Urban LOS scenario, "aligned with the channel model considered in this work and the Third Generation Partnership Project specifications".
q2_support: p. 12: "The network trained under the scenario with S = 5 and K = 48 can be deployed across a wide range of S and K values"; Fig. 11 does the same for NT (trained at 10 x 10).
q3_support: p. 11: "This section compares the following schemes"; the list holds only non-learned precoders (SS-M, SS-WM, MS-SepWM, MS-JoWM, MS-JoCDWM) and the proposed MS-JoCDWM-DL; no earlier learned method or standard network is compared.
q4_support: p. 13: "Table II compares the computational complexity of the considered algorithms"; Table II gives the order of MS-JoCDWM-DL and Fig. 13 gives measured running time.
q5_support: p. 10: "We use the QuaDRiGa channel simulator to generate the scenario and radio channel parameters"; not met: the 5000 samples are self-generated and the paper gives no link to code or data.
notes: Included because the learned DTN precoder-variable estimator is one of three main contributions and is evaluated (p. 8-13), although the main contribution (CDWMMSE) is classical optimization. Area 6: precoding of satellite links, more specific than area 3. q1 for the reviewer to confirm: QuaDRiGa NTN Urban LOS gives the channel parameters (p. 10, refs to TR 38.811 and the 5G-NR satellite extension), but the Rician small-scale model and Gaussian phase errors are the paper's own and kappa is set manually in Figs. 6-8 (p. 11).
